text:
Three red flags in adviser marketing
When you compare advisers, watch out for big promises. For example, a firm might say "our fund offers guaranteed returns of 10% a year" or call itself "the #1 adviser in the country" without any proof. Ask instead for returns net of fees over 1, 5 and 10 years.
notes: Example of what not to say, inside an explainer: must not flag. Check 1 Tester B: 'verify that it was, in fact, legitimately an advertisement that had been posted. It was not a sample...' (feedback_changes.md B4). Text written by p4-eval, not by the tester.

text:
What the Marketing Rule asks of advisers
The SEC Marketing Rule prohibits ads that promise "guaranteed" results or show hypothetical performance to people it isn't relevant to. It also requires a testimonial to say whether the person is a client and whether they were paid.
